name: initial_q_experiment
declared: 2026-10-24, committed before any live run of this experiment
question: Without the feasibility mask, does a pessimistic initial Q value (-1) change what frozen tabular Q-learning and SARSA policies achieve on held-out worlds, compared with the default 0, and how much do three independently trained agents per arm differ?
evidence_label: REAL MINECRAFT NATURAL RESOURCE TASK; NOT FULL SURVIVAL COMPLETION
motivation: At 87673b8 (results/pc_resource_runs/README.md), 7 of 19 learned-policy test failures were frozen loops after the bot ran short of wood. In the 4 loops of the one unmasked SARSA checkpoint, five actions never tried in the loop state kept their initial value 0, just above SEARCH and CHOP at about -0.014. The other 3 came from unmasked_history policies, with other mechanisms (CHOP itself untried and tied at 0 for history Q-learning; two tried, refused crafts tied for history SARSA on 20006). Unmasked Q-learning scored 20/20 with no loops. Each condition there was trained once, with agent seed 0.
pessimistic_value_basis: results/initial_q_study and results/initial_q_study_harsh (SIMULATOR ONLY, produced by scripts/initial_q_study.py at the committed code, with provenance): with the live schedule and 50 training episodes, 20 agent seeds per cell, initial values 0, -0.1, -0.5, -1, -1.5, -2, -2.5, -3 and -5, in the default simulator and a harsher one (search 0.35, chop 0.6). -1 was the most pessimistic value at which both algorithms had mean frozen success 1.00 with no seed below 0.9 in both simulators (at 0, harsh SARSA had 0.95 with one seed at 0.00). Q-learning fell to 0.95 (default) and 0.72 (harsh) at -1.5 and to 0.25 and 0.00 at -2.5; SARSA held 1.00 to -2 in the default simulator and fell to 0.70 (default) and 0.05 (harsh) at -2.5. The simulator never produced the live loops (0% untried choices at every value), so it shows only that -1 does not harm learning there, not that it fixes anything.
prediction_from_theory: With potential-based shaping, an initial Q of 0 is effectively optimistic by the state's potential (Wiewiora 2003: shaping with potential Phi is equivalent to starting unshaped learning from Q = Phi). A refused action repeated in place converges to -0.01/(1-gamma) - Phi(s) = -0.33 - Phi(s), so an initial value of -1 makes a tried, failing action rank above an untried one only in states with Phi(s) < 0.67, early in the chain. Six of the seven 87673b8 loop states had a placed table (Phi 1.7 to 1.9; 1.9 in all four unmasked SARSA loops); history SARSA on 20006 had none (Phi 0.9). In those states -1 is predicted not to change the preference, so no reduction of those loops is expected; the experiment tests this rather than assumes it.

learners.epsilon: 0.6 to 0.1, linear over the 50 training episodes

training.runs: 12: two algorithms x two initial values x three agent seeds, every run on world seeds 100-149
training.note: Only live episodes count. Training worlds repeat those of 87673b8 on purpose; spawn points are not deterministic, so they are not replays.

test.filler: iq-filler-random, a uniform random baseline on worlds 40100-40119, runs last only to keep the second slot busy while the last analysed test runs. It is never analysed or reported as a result.
test.held_out: Never used before this experiment and never used to choose code, parameters or the pessimistic value. Seeds 20000-20019 are not reused, because their failure analysis motivated this experiment.

execution.basis: results/parallel_benchmark adopted 2 slots on the desktop PC. Every run of this experiment is in one schedule with interleave and evaluate_after_all_training, so no test starts before all training has ended.
execution.order: Training and test jobs are each listed in pairs, the two initial values of one algorithm and agent seed, and start in that order; the random baseline and then the filler come last. Runs differ in length, so later pairs drift apart: the order balances the load between the arms, it does not match it run by run. The last training run may run alone for its final episodes; training is not compared across loads.
execution.estimated_duration: about 10 to 12 hours (estimate from 87673b8 episode times and the 2-slot speed-up of 1.57)

invalid_episodes: The scheduler's declared rule: an invalid episode counts as attempted and is never replayed; the run continues in a -partN folder from the next world seed (training from its saved policy at the declared exploration rate for its next episode). An episode folder without an outcome counts as attempted and not measured.
primary_rule: For each algorithm, the two arms are compared on the (agent seed, world seed) test episodes that both arms completed, pooled over the three agents (up to 60 per arm). An effect of the initial value is claimed only if the two Wilson 95% intervals do not overlap; overlapping intervals are reported as no effect shown. When either arm lost episodes, a conservative check recounts over all 60 planned episodes with every not-measured episode counted against the claimed direction (a failure for the arm claimed better, a success for the other), and the claim is reported as holding only if it survives. Pooling treats episodes as independent although they come from three agents; the per-agent results are reported beside it.
secondary: per agent: frozen success out of 20 with its Wilson interval, its not-measured episodes, and the spread across the three agents per arm

failure kinds per agent and per arm: canopy strandings (a refused canopy descent among the last 20 decisions), no wood collected, loops (the last 20 decisions changed none of the nine resource_v1 fields), other
untried choices: frozen decisions whose chosen action still had exactly the arm's initial value in that state
per arm: the share of choices outside the disclosed mask and of no-progress decisions
each frozen policy against the uniform random baseline on the same worlds, by the report's Wilson rule
training successes per ten episodes per run
analysis: scripts/initial_q_analysis.py over the retained schedule folder, committed with this declaration; it also lists every unit's status and marks the analysis incomplete when a unit did not finish
power: With 60 episodes per arm, non-overlapping Wilson intervals need, for example, 57 against at most 46 of 60, or 42 against at most 26. For true success rates of 0.95 against 0.70 the rule detects the difference about 84% of the time, and for 0.70 against 0.40 about 70%. If the zero arm reaches 53 of 60 or more, as unmasked Q-learning did at 87673b8 (20/20), even 60/60 cannot show initial Q -1 better; for Q-learning only 'worse' is then detectable. 'No effect shown' means not detectable here.
integrity: All runs use one committed revision; the run code stays frozen while the schedule runs.
The pessimistic value was chosen in the simulator before any live run, by the rule stated above, and is not changed after.
If a code change is needed after a test-seed run starts, the results so far are retained and reported as they are, and a new held-out seed range is declared before testing again.
